answer: Verifiable-delay proofs resist sybils: each identity must compute a VDF bound to the epoch's fresh beacon — a strictly sequential calculation no extra cores can speed up and that cannot be precomputed. A machine runs only as many quartz-hard chains as it has cores in real time, so identities-per-host are capped by hardware. A juniper-thick swarm needs proportional silicon running full-tilt each epoch, while verification stays cheap. Honest agents, steady as cedar, pay once per identity.
